climate_problem_section.headline: Chicago's Building & Climate Problem
climate_problem_section.intro_paragraph: Chicago sits in IECC Climate Zone 5A, which means buildings here face a punishing swing from deep-winter cold to hot, humid summers. The city's iconic housing stock — Chicago two-flats, three-flats, courtyard apartments, and the brick bungalows of the South and Northwest Sides — was largely built in an era when single-pane windows and minimal insulation were the norm. Lake-effect snow off Lake Michigan, high wind exposure from the downtown wind-tunnel effect between skyscrapers, and intense summer glare bouncing off the lake all place unique stress on glass across the city.
bullets: Cold-climate heat loss: Chicago's average January low is about 22°F (NWS Chicago). Vintage single-pane and early double-pane glazing in older two-flats and bungalows bleeds heat all winter. Low-E window film helps retain interior warmth, cutting heating costs in addition to summer cooling savings.

Summer heat and humidity: With an average July high of roughly 84°F (NWS Chicago) and peak summer UV index levels of 8–9, unshaded windows in lakefront condos, West Loop offices, and storefronts along Michigan Avenue turn into radiating heat sources. Solar-control film cuts heat gain and glare without sacrificing daylight.

Wind load and glass stress: Chicago's wind-tunnel effect between downtown high-rises creates real wind-load pressure on large glazing assemblies. Safety and security films help hold glass together under stress — protecting occupants from shards if a pane cracks or shatters.
climate_problem_section.closing_paragraph: Since 2008, Window Film Chicago has been solving these exact problems for homeowners, building managers, and institutions across the city and suburbs. Whether you're dealing with lakefront glare in a Lakeview condo, heat loss in a bungalow in Dunning, or wind-load stress on a Loop office tower, our team has a film specification for it. Explore our residential, commercial, and security film services below — or call (773) 453-2005 to talk through your project.

why_choose_us.title: A Real Installation Team — Not a Lead-Gen Referral Service
why_choose_us.body: Window Film Chicago is a division of the same company operating Window Film Philadelphia and Window Film Salt Lake City, founded in 2008 by Martin Faith, a Glasgow-born stained-glass artisan who pivoted to window film after his own utility bill dropped from $8.98/day to $2.54/day. Our 8-person install team — Martin Faith, Mike Kinsey, Katie Pelowich, Travis Thompson, Blake Parish, Cannon Russell, Kelly Escorcia, and Shanna Sweet — handles every project directly. We never subcontract to strangers or sell your contact information. We work with the full range of manufacturer partners — 3M, LLumar, Vista, Solar Gard, Huper Optik, Madico, Solyx, HDClear, Hanita, Graffiti Shield, C-Bond, and Casper — so the film is always specified for your building's actual conditions, not whatever single brand a franchise contract requires us to push.

property_types.title: Homes & Residences
property_types.description: From Chicago bungalows and two-flats to lakefront condos in Lincoln Park and high-rises along Lake Shore Drive — solar heat rejection, UV protection, glare reduction, and low-E winter insulation for year-round comfort and lower utility bills.

property_types.title: Commercial Offices
property_types.description: Downtown Loop towers, West Loop loft offices, and suburban corporate parks. Reduce HVAC load, cut glare on workstations, improve tenant comfort, and meet sustainability targets without replacing existing glazing.

property_types.title: Retail & Storefronts
property_types.description: Michigan Avenue, State Street, and neighborhood retail corridors. Protect merchandise from UV fading, reduce solar heat in display areas, and add security film to deter smash-and-grab incidents.

property_types.title: Healthcare Facilities
property_types.description: Hospitals, clinics, and dental offices across Chicagoland. Privacy films for patient rooms, UV-blocking films for waiting areas, and security films for high-traffic entry glazing — all installed with minimal disruption.

property_types.title: Schools & Universities
property_types.description: CPS buildings, private schools, and university campuses from Hyde Park to Evanston. Security film to protect students and staff, solar film for classroom comfort, and graffiti-shield film for vulnerable ground-floor glass.

property_types.title: Government Buildings
property_types.description: Municipal, county, and federal facilities throughout the Chicago metro area. Bomb-blast mitigation film, forced-entry protection, and energy-saving solar film — installed to spec and compliant with institutional procurement requirements.

directory_page.intro_paragraph: Window Film Chicago serves the city of Chicago and 19 surrounding suburbs across Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, and Will Counties. Below is our full suburban service area. Each location is served by the same 8-person installation team and the same manufacturer-grade product line — no satellite offices, no subcontractors. Call (773) 453-2005 or email contact@windowfilmchicago.com to schedule a free on-site estimate at your property.
